comment: Cross-implementation anchor for the invariant-report contract (kernel/src/invariant-report.ts): what a run may state about its own invariant checks, and how to digest one so a re-verification can cite the failure it answers. Rules a second implementation must reproduce, stated here so it need not read the TypeScript: (1) schemaVersion is exactly `iterate.invariant-report/0.1`. (2) `outcome` is `pass|fail|error`. (3) `checks` is 1..256 entries, each an object with required `name` (1..256 chars), required `kind` in `ensure|command|refused`, required `ok` boolean, and optional `detail` (<=4096); no other keys. (4) THE ONE RULE THAT MATTERS: `outcome` must follow from `checks`. `pass` requires every check to have ok true. `fail` requires at least one check with ok false. `error` is unconstrained. A report that says pass over a failed check is refused by both validators — the JSON Schema expresses this with `allOf`/`if`/`then`/`contains`, so a schema-only consumer refuses it too. (5) `kind` `refused` means the runner declined to execute a configured command because it carries shell metacharacters or is empty; it is a violation, so a report whose only failing check was refused is `fail`, never `error`. `error` is reserved for checks that could not be evaluated at all, and it produces no re-verification request. (6) `round` (>=1) and `durationMs` (>=0) are optional integers. (7) The digest is `iv_` + sha256 of the canonical JSON form: UTF-16-code-unit-sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace, arrays in order, strings as JSON escapes them; numbers use the host's shortest roundtrip form (integral values print without a fraction). (8) A re-verification request is `iterate.reverification/0.1` with `trigger.kind` exactly `invariant`, `trigger.reportDigest` matching `^iv_[0-9a-f]{64}$`, and `targets` carrying at least one of `recipeSteps` (1..64), `dimensions` (1..64 kebab-case ids <=64 chars), `operationIds` (1..64 matching `^op_[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$`); an empty target set is refused, by `anyOf` in the schema and by `superRefine` in the validator. PROVENANCE: every name, kind and detail string below was captured from `iterate_harness.defensive.invariants.check_invariants` running against the real repo — the ensure entries are the config's own `invariants.ensure` plus a file the run does not have, the command label is the real `<module>:<command>` format, the `exit 1 | ...` tail is real npm output truncated the way the runner truncates it (last three lines, joined by ' | '), and `python:ruff check src/ ; rm -rf /` is the metacharacter case the runner refuses with the exact string it uses. The runner records only violations plus a count, so the ok=true entries here are the configured check names minus the violating ones — that is how a producer derives `checks`, not an invention for this fixture.
